result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers swap the trapezoids for bars on a shared zero baseline, use all five counts unchanged, and get every percentage right. Answer B separates the weakest rate (setup to paid) from the largest absolute loss (download to account), but it never says where the data comes from. Answer A includes the unit, what the percentages are relative to, a source and date line, and a caution against over-claiming, and its advice is a bit tighter, so A edges ahead. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers redesign the chart as bars on a shared left baseline, use all five counts unchanged, and get every percentage right (63.7%, 54.4%, 91.9%, 27.8%; 8.9% overall), with setup to paid flagged as the weakest step. B wins on rubric item 5: it adds a source, period and as-of note and labels the unit as users, while A explains what the percentages are relative to but never says where the data comes from. A has an advantage in also pointing out the largest absolute loss (4,500 users, download to account), but B's headline claim about the paywall and its extra section on keeping the funnel shape are minor weaknesses.
